newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-FIXTURES THIS WEEKEND IN THE SPANISH CHAMPIONSHIP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FIXTURES THIS WEEKEND IN THE SPANISH CHAMPIONSHIP.

text.p: Games scheduled for the weekend in the Spanish league championship (league positions in parentheses, kick off times gmt:
Playing Saturday:
Real Betis (4) vs Sevilla (21) kick off 1830 gmt

Defeat in the Seville derby game would almost certainly cost Sevilla relegation, or Betis a shot at second place and with it a European Cup berth. The clash has been enlivened by Betis' weak form and Sevilla's recent revival.
Playing Sunday:
Real Sociedad (7) vs Atletico Madrid (5) 1600

Atletico scored a convincing 3-2 triumph in the postponed game at Tenerife on Thursday, and have guaranteed a UEFA Cup place, unlike Javier Irureta's Real Sociedad, who welcome back Nigerian midfielder Mutiu Adepojo from injury.
Extremadura (17) vs Athletic Bilbao (8) 1600
Extremadura have performed a Houdini-like escape act, but face a very tough run-in, while Athletic badly need the points in their bid for a UEFA Cup place.
Espanyol (15) vs Tenerife (9) 1600
Espanyol's teenage goalscorer Raul Tamudo is out injured for the game against a Tenerife side that looked out of touch in Thursday's 3-2 home defeat by Atletico Madrid.
Rayo Vallecano (18) vs Logrones (22) 1700
Even with a draw Logrones could easily end Sunday in the second division, while Rayo Vallecano hope not to go the same way after badly fading in the second half of the season.
Real Madrid (1) vs Valladolid (6) 1700

Real Madrid teenage sensation Raul Gonzalez is trying to shake off a nagging groin injury for a game against Spain's surprise outfit, who have only taken points home from four visits to the mighty Santiago Bernabeu stadium.
Hercules (20) vs Valencia (10) 1700

Valencia haven't won a league game at their neighbours for over 50 years, partially through Hercules' absence from the first division. Hercules will hope to have captain Pascual Parra back from injury.
Racing Santander (11) vs Zaragoza (14) 1700
Racing will be without injured Serbian midfielder Dejan Petkovic, while Zaragoza hope to force the lifting of the two-game suspension on Brazilian player Gilmar.
Oviedo (16) vs Compostela (12) 1700
Compostela have never won at Oviedo in the first division and have been hit by a renewal in the long-running conflict between coach Javier Vazquez and chairman Jose Maria Caneda.
Deportivo Coruna (3) vs Sporting Gijon (19) 1730

Deportivo have never lost at home to Sporting, and are hoping to see the suspension of star Brazilian midfielder Rivaldo lifted. Deportivo will need to pressurise Barcelona in their bid for Spain's second European Cup place.
Playing Monday:
Celta Vigo (13) vs Barcelona (2) 1930

Barcelona are on a high after Wednesday's Cup Winner's Cup victory, but will be without Albert Ferrer, Luis Figo and Hristo Stoichkov because of suspension, while Celta will drop Russian midfielder Alexander Mostovoi for repeated indiscipline.
